title: China's Biggest Lake Sits 3,260 m Up — a 360 km Loop | China Travel Expert
description:
China's biggest lake sits about 3,260 metres above sea level — and the road that loops around it runs roughly 360 km.

That's Qinghai Lake, a saline alpine lake on the Tibetan Plateau with a surface area over 4,500 square kilometres (about 4,543 km² as of 2020) — the largest lake in China. Every summer the shoreline fills with gold rapeseed (canola) flowers, peaking around mid-July. The full loop is a classic China road trip: drivers can circle it in a long day, while cyclists usually take three to four days. It's high country, so give yourself time to adjust to the altitude.

🧭 Expert Tip: Aim for mid-July if you want the rapeseed fields in bloom, base yourself in Xining, and take the altitude seriously — 3,260 m is high enough to feel it, so ease into the first day and keep water and altitude meds handy.
